title: src/mixer.rs: weigh the models' predictions by what each has been worth, in the context at hand, instead of averaging them
context: Make the mixer learn. Today Mixer::mix averages the models' stretched predictions, every model counting the same, and Mixer::update learns nothing. Give each model a weight, chosen by a small context (the bit's place in the byte, for instance), moved after each bit by the error of the mixed prediction; keep it working for any number of inputs, since models are added as files with no list. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least half a percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes: the message 3,544,012 (one order-2 model, 2.84 bits a character) and the program 1,346,472, of which about 1.3 MB is the frame around it, which you cannot touch. A mixer's code is small; its gain is paid in full once more models are in. Work in src/mixer.rs (new, mix, update). The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/models/: a new model of order 3 in its own file
context: Add a model of order 3: the three bytes before, with the bits of the byte known so far, choosing one count, as the order-2 model does for two. Put it in one new file of src/models/ (the build finds it by its name; read the order-2 file for what a model gives: OUTPUTS, new, predict, update). The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes, the message 3,544,012 and the program 1,346,472; the program's own code is a few hundred to a few thousand bytes a model, small against what a model takes off the message. A model of order 3 was measured to bring the total to 4,334,340 (11.4 % fewer) at 0.8 s to encode and 2.3 s to decode with 79 MB, with the mixer still averaging. Use a table sized to what the corpus needs, or hash the context: memory counts. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. title: src/transform.rs: rewrite the text before modelling (capitals, curly quotes and dashes) and back exactly
context: Rewrite the text before it is modelled, and back exactly after it is decoded: the corpus is English prose and verse in UTF-8, with the plays' speakers' names and headings in capitals, curly quotes and dashes of three bytes each, and many frequent words. Pick one idea (for example a marker for a capital with the letter lowered, or one byte for a curly quote) and write forward and inverse for it; today both return their input. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. The message is 3,544,012 bytes of today's 4,890,484 total, the program 1,346,472: a table or a word list you write is counted in the program, so it must pay for itself. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/logistic.rs, src/coder.rs, src/frame.rs: more than twelve bits of probability where nearly sure, and a shorter end of message
context: One idea: let the coder use more than twelve bits of probability where the models are nearly sure, and end the message with fewer bytes. Today the probability handed to the coder is out of 4096 and Predictor::predict clamps it between 1 and 4095; Scale::squash and Scale::stretch work on that scale; Encoder::finish writes the end of the message. The three files change together, so this is one task and no other task names them. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least a quarter of one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes: the message 3,544,012, the program 1,346,472. The decoder must stay in step with the encoder bit for bit. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/models/: how the order-2 model's counts adapt (a rate that slows as evidence grows)
context: One idea: how the order-2 model's count adapts. Today each count of 16 bits moves a sixteenth of the way towards each bit (RATE 4), whatever it has seen. Let it adapt faster while a context is new and slower as evidence grows (a small counter kept with the count), or keep two speeds at once and give both as predictions. Work in the order-2 file of src/models/ (new, predict, update). The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise.
